edition: Newton, Principia, Andrew Motte trans., 1729 (Wikisource); Axioms, or Laws of Motion, Law I.

figures.caption: Law I — Every body perseveres in its state of rest, or of uniform motion in a right line, unless it is compelled to change that state by forces impress'd thereon.

text.latex: Every body perseveres in \textcolor{rest}{a state of rest}, or of \textcolor{uniform}{uniform motion in a right line}, \     unless compelled to change that state. A body left to itself does nothing on its own — it neither \     slows, speeds, nor turns. The sole agent that alters this perseverance is a \textcolor{force}{force impress'd thereon}, \     so that with $\sum \vec{F} = 0$ we have $\vec{v} = \text{const}$: velocity, in both speed and direction, is preserved.

\textcolor{top}{A top}, whose parts by their \textcolor{cohesion}{cohesion} are perpetually drawn aside from rectilinear motions, \     does not cease its rotation otherwise than as it is retarded by \textcolor{air}{the air}. Each part is forever pulled \     inward from the straight line it would take, yet the whole endures because no force impels it to stop. \     Remove the \textcolor{air}{air} and the top would spin forever, its angular speed unchanged, $\omega = \text{const}$.

The greater bodies of the \textcolor{bodies}{planets and comets}, meeting with less resistance in \textcolor{free}{more free spaces}, \     preserve the \textcolor{motions}{motions both progressive and circular} for a much longer time. In the near-void between \     the stars scarcely anything retards them, so their onward drift and their orbital turning both endure. \     These are the law's strongest witnesses: across immense times, $\vec{v}_{\text{prog}}$ and $\vec{\omega}_{\text{orb}}$ hold nearly constant.

\textcolor{proj}{Projectiles} persevere in their motions, so far as they are not retarded by the \textcolor{resist}{resistance of the air}, \     or impelled downwards by the \textcolor{gravity}{force of gravity}. A stone or a cannonball, once flung, would fly straight \     on forever were these two forces absent — shot fast enough horizontally, it would circle the whole Earth. \     What we see as a falling arc is only the \textcolor{proj}{projectile's} straight perseverance bent by $\vec{a} = \vec{g} + \tfrac{\vec{F}_{\text{air}}}{m}$.
